title: Reading stack traces
learningObjectives: Explain reading stack traces and diagnose or handle JavaScript errors safely.

understand.concept: A stack trace shows the sequence of function calls associated with an error and often includes source locations and line numbers. Read the first relevant application frame, inspect the failing expression, and trace the call path to understand how the program reached it.
understand.whyItMatters: Stack traces reduce guesswork by identifying where an error occurred and which functions led there. Source maps can map compiled output back to original source in supported development setups.
understand.analogy: A stack trace is like a route history showing which steps led to the failure.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript parsing, execution, and exception propagation follow language and runtime rules.

explain.narrative: The error occurs because a string does not provide the expected toFixed method. The stack trace shows the call path through format and calculate.

examples.explanation: The error occurs because a string does not provide the expected toFixed method. The stack trace shows the call path through format and calculate.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console or page demonstrates the error, stack, or handled result described.

practise.guidedTask: Trigger a runtime error inside nested functions. Read the stack trace and identify the first application line that needs inspection.
practise.independentTask: Create a small example with a deliberate error or invalid input. Diagnose it using developer tools and provide useful, non-sensitive feedback.
hints: Separate syntax, runtime, and logic errors.
Read the first relevant application frame in a stack trace.
Do not silently swallow exceptions or expose secrets.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Reading stack traces</title></head><body>
<script>function calculate(value){return format(value);}function format(value){return value.toFixed(2);}try{console.log(calculate('not a number'));}catch(error){console.error(error.stack);}</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: What information does a stack trace provide?
options: The call sequence and source location associated with an error
questions.answer: The call sequence and source location associated with an error
questions.explanation: A stack trace helps locate the failing call and the functions that led to it.

questions.prompt: What is a good error-handling practice?
options: Handle errors at meaningful boundaries and give safe feedback
Expose full stack traces and secrets to users
questions.answer: Handle errors at meaningful boundaries and give safe feedback
questions.explanation: Good error handling supports debugging while protecting users from sensitive internal details.
